newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-CLAY COURT KING MUSTER FALTERS AHEAD OF FRENCH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CLAY COURT KING MUSTER FALTERS AHEAD OF FRENCH OPEN.

text.p: Top seed and world number five Thomas Muster suffered another blow ahead of next week's French Open, when he crashed out of the quarter-finals of the $425,000 St.Poelten Grand Prix on Thursday.
After losing 6-3 7-6 to Australia's Patrick Rafter in just over an hour, the former 'King of Clay' expressed little confidence he could reclaim the Roland Garros title he surrendered last year.
"In Paris I have to make sure I improve my game in every match I play... that is, if I get to play a lot of matches," he said. "I had a lot of chances today which I failed to use."
Muster, a dominating force on clay in 1995 and 1996 when he won 111 matches, has failed to win a single tournament on the surface this season and has lost the invincibility opponents once feared.
Even so, seventh-seed Rafter was delighted with his performance.
He said: "It is good for me to go into the French Open with a win against Muster. It gives me a lot of confidence.
"Everyone knows Muster is not playing well on clay at the moment. But still you have to make sure you play well against him, if you don't then he beats you.
"I knew the only way to beat him was to come into the net a lot and play serve and volley," added Rafter, ranked 33 in the world and the only remaining seed in St.Poelten.

He next meets the winner of the quarter-final match between Sjeng Schalken of the Netherlands and Sweden's Magnus Norman, which was halted due to rain finely poised at a set apiece 6-1 1-6 and will resume Friday morning.

In other quarter-final encounters, Slovakia's Dominik Hrbaty beat Moroccan Karim Alami 6-1 6-2, while Marcelo Filippini of Uruguay defeated Swede Tomas Nydahl 7-5 6-1 in a match which was interrupted twice by heavy rain.
